name: Change Canvas — Embedding a New Way of Working at Maasland Verzekeringen
description: A four-round, intermediate change-leadership simulation set inside Maasland Verzekeringen N.V., a Utrecht-based mid-market Dutch insurer (2,100 staff, €640M gross written premium) rolling a new low-code, team-based way of working across 18 claims and underwriting teams (≈600 people). It is 14 April 2026 and the rollout has stalled: the company repeated its historic pattern — a launch town-hall, one training session, then silence — and adoption sits at just 34% daily active use against an 80% board target, the resistance index has climbed from 28 to 51/100, engagement is down 14 points, and €410,000 of the €1.2M change budget is already spent (≈€790,000 remains) with platform-licence renewal and a CFO go/no-go in month 10. As the Change Lead reporting to the COO, the learner applies Woody van Olffen's Change Canvas logic — designing and monitoring change across the rational case, the emotional and political reality, capability building, and reinforcement — rather than announcing and assuming. Round 1 (Diagnose): separate the three root-cause gaps behind the 34% stall — the 'why' (no compelling case for change), the 'ability' (one-off training), and the 'reinforcement' (managers not modelling the behaviour) — and pick the highest-leverage stakeholders to engage first. Round 2 (Plan): design the intervention portfolio under the remaining budget by choosing intervention intensity (light comms+e-learning / medium workshops+coaching / heavy embedded agents+manager bootcamps), a communication cadence (one-off broadcast vs. sustained two-way rhythm), and the engagement order — the discovery being that front-loading line-manager enablement before frontline training bends the adoption curve more than any volume of communication. Round 3 (Decide): sequence the 12 remaining teams into waves and commit spend, choosing whether to stabilise the six struggling live teams first (rescue) or push forward (momentum), while respecting finite change-agent and coaching capacity so heavy intensity cannot be lavished on every team. Round 4 (Recover): absorb two shocks — a vocal middle-manager coalition questioning the programme in a town-hall and a regulatory deadline pulling 20% of frontline time for a month — protect adoption, convert sceptical managers into advocates, install a reinforcement mechanism (peer champions, sponsor visibility, metrics in daily routines), and defend the platform renewal to the board. The scoring rewards diagnosing the reinforcement gap, manager-first sequencing, dosage matched to readiness, rescuing early failures, treating resistance as signal, and designing reinforcement — and measurably punishes the five classic errors: broadcast bias, frontline-before-managers, uniform heavy intensity, momentum over rescue, and launch-as-success. Final KPIs track daily-active adoption (%), the resistance index (/100), engagement change (points), budget remaining (€K) and modelled time-to-embed (months).
view:
14 April 2026 · Maasland Verzekeringen N.V. · Utrecht · the rollout has stalled

Change Canvas

You are the Change Lead at a Dutch insurer rolling a new team-based way of working across 18 teams. Twelve weeks in, adoption is stuck at 34% against an 80% board target, resistance has climbed to 51/100, and €410K of the €1.2M budget is gone. Sequence interventions, set the communication cadence, and engage the right stakeholders first — before the platform licence renewal forces a go/no-go.

Teams in scope 18 · ≈600 people
Live / remaining 6 live · 12 to come
Window 9 months · renewal month 10
Cancel threshold < 60% network-wide
Round 1 of 4 Month 0 · diagnose the stall
Daily Active Adoption
34%
Target 80% by month 9 · cancel below 60% · historic plateau ~40%
Resistance Index
51
0–100, lower is safer · up from 28 before launch
Engagement Change
−14
Points vs. baseline among live users · attrition rising in reverted teams
Budget Remaining
€790K
Of €1.2M ring-fenced · €410K already spent on licences + launch
Modelled time-to-embed (lower is better · target ≈5 months/team) 7.0 mo
🗂️
Round 1 — Diagnose: map the change landscape

Your Decisions This Round

Diagnostic focus on the gap you named: 35%
Spend front-loaded into managers: 20%
This share is charged to the remaining budget, on top of the intensity you choose.
Facilitator (your COO sponsor & the steering committee)
Twelve weeks in: 34% adoption against an 80% target, resistance up to 51, two teams back on their spreadsheets, and €410K already spent, mostly on licences and the launch event. Ingrid Molenaar, who runs claims operations, has said she will recommend reverting the whole division if she cannot see real adoption in her own area within two months. The platform licence renews in month 10. Decide what the 34% means before you spend another euro.

Round-by-Round Record

Adoption, Resistance & Engagement Trajectory

text.en: Diagnose an adoption stall by separating awareness, capability and reinforcement gaps and justify the diagnosis from adoption, resistance and engagement data
text.es: Diagnosticar un estancamiento en la adopción separando brechas de conocimiento, de capacidad y de refuerzo, y justificar el diagnóstico con datos de adopción, resistencia y compromiso

text.en: Sequence stakeholder enablement so that those who must model and reinforce a behaviour are equipped before those who must perform it
text.es: Secuenciar la capacitación de los grupos de interés para que quienes deben ejemplificar y reforzar una conducta estén preparados antes que quienes deben ejecutarla

text.en: Ration a fixed change budget by matching intervention intensity to team readiness and defend the teams where less support is the right answer
text.es: Racionar un presupuesto de cambio fijo ajustando la intensidad de la intervención a la preparación de cada equipo, y defender los equipos donde menos apoyo es la respuesta correcta

text.en: Interpret resistance as diagnostic information and design a conversion strategy for a sceptical coalition rather than an authority response
text.es: Interpretar la resistencia como información diagnóstica y diseñar una estrategia de conversión para una coalición escéptica en lugar de una respuesta de autoridad

text.en: Design reinforcement mechanisms that sustain behaviour after programme support ends and evaluate them against the organisation's historic decay
text.es: Diseñar mecanismos de refuerzo que sostengan la conducta una vez retirado el apoyo del programa y evaluarlos frente al deterioro histórico de la organización

name.en: Answering the stall with more communication
name.es: Responder al estancamiento con más comunicación

lure.en: The launch was one town-hall and one email campaign, so too little communication is the reading closest to hand, and a second broadcast is fast and costs nothing from the budget
lure.es: El lanzamiento fue una asamblea y una campaña de correo, así que la falta de comunicación es la lectura más a mano, y un segundo anuncio es rápido y no consume presupuesto

consequence.en: Adoption does not move and the resistance index keeps rising: volume does not close a gap that sits in what line managers do, and the time to embed a team lengthens
consequence.es: La adopción no se mueve y el índice de resistencia sigue subiendo: el volumen no cierra una brecha que está en lo que hacen los mandos, y el tiempo de arraigo por equipo se alarga

source.ref: TN §7 Q1 (awareness reading) and Q5 (Round 1's 'communicate harder'); §11 takeaway 3; TN-Exhibit 2 (broadcastBias)

name.en: Training the frontline before enabling their managers
name.es: Formar a la primera línea antes de habilitar a sus mandos

lure.en: The frontline is where the work happens and is the larger population; enabling four hundred people is the long pole, and starting the long pole first is standard project logic
lure.es: La primera línea es donde se hace el trabajo y es el grupo más grande; habilitar a cuatrocientas personas es la tarea más larga, y empezar por la más larga es lógica de proyecto habitual

consequence.en: Trained staff meet a manager who does not use the workflow; the manager's signal wins and adoption falls back every round toward the historic 40% plateau
consequence.es: El personal formado se encuentra con un mando que no usa el flujo; la señal del mando se impone y la adopción retrocede cada ronda hacia la meseta histórica del 40%

source.ref: TN §5.2; §7 Q2 (argument for frontline-first); TN-Exhibit 3 (multiplier collapse); TN-Exhibit 4 run C

name.en: Launching new waves past the two reverted teams
name.es: Lanzar nuevas olas dejando atrás a los dos equipos que revirtieron

lure.en: Stabilising the six live teams costs schedule, and the renewal date in month ten does not move; new waves look like progress to the board
lure.es: Estabilizar los seis equipos en marcha cuesta calendario, y la fecha de renovación del mes diez no se mueve; las nuevas olas parecen avance ante el consejo

consequence.en: A visibly reverted team is a broadcast to the twelve teams that have not started: resistance rises, the new waves land worse and the achievable ending is capped
consequence.es: Un equipo que revierte a la vista es un mensaje para los doce equipos que no han empezado: sube la resistencia, las nuevas olas arraigan peor y el final alcanzable queda limitado

source.ref: TN §5.5 (discontinuance as a broadcast); §7 Q3 (rescue versus momentum); §11 takeaway 5

name.es: Apoyo intensivo para todos los equipos

lure.en: Uniform heavy support feels rigorous (we only get one shot) and gives the largest adoption gain of the design phase
lure.es: El apoyo intensivo uniforme parece riguroso (solo tenemos una oportunidad) y da la mayor ganancia de adopción de la fase de diseño

consequence.en: Finite change-agent capacity and budget run out before the last waves; the teams reached last get nothing and revert, because intensity was never rationed against readiness
consequence.es: La capacidad finita de agentes de cambio y el presupuesto se agotan antes de las últimas olas; los equipos del final se quedan sin apoyo y revierten, porque la intensidad nunca se racionó según la preparación

source.ref: TN §5.4 (dosage and readiness); §7 Q3 ('Heavy everywhere, we only get one shot'); §11 takeaway 4; §13 (heavy everywhere)

name.es: Declarar el éxito en cada puesta en marcha

lure.en: A celebration at go-live recognises the effort, costs little and matches how every earlier Maasland rollout ended
lure.es: Una celebración en la puesta en marcha reconoce el esfuerzo, cuesta poco y coincide con cómo terminó cada despliegue anterior de Maasland

consequence.en: The celebration signals that the effort is over; with nothing left in the daily routine once the change agents leave, adoption decays toward the 40% plateau
consequence.es: La celebración indica que el esfuerzo ha terminado; sin nada en la rutina diaria cuando se van los agentes de cambio, la adopción decae hacia la meseta del 40%

source.ref: TN §5.6 (Kotter 1995, declaring victory too soon); §7 Q5; §11 takeaway 7
